title: Ukraine Recovery Conference series begins in Lugano and continues through London, Berlin and Rome
body:
The Ukraine Recovery Conference is an annual international gathering focused on financing and planning Ukraine's reconstruction. The first took place in Lugano, Switzerland, on 4 and 5 July 2022. Ukraine's prime minister reported infrastructure losses above 100 billion US dollars, and a draft three-stage recovery framework put reconstruction costs at 750 billion dollars. The Lugano Declaration condemned Russia's aggression and backed Ukraine's territorial integrity.

The second conference was held in London on 21 and 22 June 2023. Ukraine's prime minister requested 7 billion dollars in aid, and the European Commission proposed a new Ukraine Facility providing up to 50 billion euros over four years, from 2024 to 2027.

The third conference took place in Berlin on 11 and 12 June 2024, and the fourth in Rome on 10 and 11 July 2025. The Wikipedia article summarising the series, which is the source for these dates and figures, gives no pledge totals for Berlin or Rome in the text reviewed here. The conferences are separate from the World Bank-led Rapid Damage and Needs Assessments, whose estimates of reconstruction costs are discussed at them, and they bring together governments, international financial institutions, the private sector and civil society.
